transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... I keep hearing voices, like clear as somebody standing right there in my little studio. It’ll be quiet, nobody there, and I hear them saying my name, and saying my work is being judged. I do personal care work, you know, and people can be particular about things, but this is when I’m home, when the house is quiet. It just keeps happening, and it’s got me scared.
Do you find it hard to understand what the voices are saying or do they seem to make sense to you?

They make sense, mostly. I mean, I can hear them clear, like somebody’s right there in my studio with me, not muffled or anything. They say my name, and they talk like my work is being judged… and that gets to me because I do personal care, and you know, people watch how you do things, whether the bed is made right or you helped them the right way. But this is when I’m home and it’s quiet, nobody there, and I still hear it.
Do the voices ever tell you to do something?

They don’t exactly say, “Go do this,” not like that. It’s more them saying my name and going on about my work being judged, like somebody’s watching how I do things. And that gets in my head because with personal care, people do notice every little thing, you know, like if you folded something wrong or didn’t set a cup where they like it… but this is when I’m home in my studio and nobody’s there.
Do you believe that people are actually watching you or judging your work when you're alone in your studio?

Yes… I mean, I know how it sounds when I say it out loud, but yes. I got it in my head that the other home-care agency, and some folks from the library too, were watching what I was doing. Not just my work work, but my paintings and even my client papers, like they were trying to take something from me, some chance that was supposed to be mine.

People told me, “That doesn’t make sense,” and I heard them, but I still knew it. Like when you’ve seen how people look at your things, you know? I used to go to the library and I’d see who was sitting where, and then I’d come home and think about my papers, my paintings stacked up, and it all connected in my mind. So yes, even alone in my studio, it feels like they’re watching and judging.
Do you find that your thoughts are sometimes difficult to follow or that you have trouble expressing what you're trying to say?

I don’t know… maybe sometimes, but I don’t really notice it like that. I know what I’m trying to say in my head, and then when I start talking it kind of goes another way, like I’ll remember something from work or the library or something somebody said, and then I’m over there instead of where I started.

But I mean, I’m still trying to answer you. It’s just… my thoughts don’t always line up neat, I guess. Sometimes people tell me, “What do you mean?” and I have to go back.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when you're talking or thinking?

Yes, that happens a lot. It’s like my mind won’t stay on one thing. I’ll be thinking, okay, I need to remember a client’s medicine, and then it jumps to whether I paid the rent, and then all of a sudden I’m thinking of a title for one of my paintings, or there’s a song on and I feel like there’s some message in it, and I’m trying to catch all of it at once.

It runs fast, too fast sometimes. Like I can’t slow it down enough to make it make sense when I’m talking, so I end up going all over.
Do you feel like your thoughts are often disorganized or hard to make sense of, even when you're not feeling stressed or anxious?

Yeah… even when I’m not upset, it still happens. It’s like my thoughts take off before I can catch them. One minute I’m thinking about a client’s medicine, and then I’m thinking, did I pay the rent, and then I’m thinking of a title for a painting I didn’t even finish yet, and then a song comes on and I’m trying to figure out what it means.

And I know that sounds like I’m just distracted, but it’s faster than that. It’s like everything is running at the same time, and I can’t slow it down enough to make it come out right. Sometimes I start talking and by the time I get to the end, I’m not even where I meant to be.
Have you ever had a period of time where your thoughts were disorganized and you heard voices at the same time?

Yeah… that’s kind of why I came in. My thoughts get all tangled up, and then I hear them — the voices — clear, like somebody is standing right there in my little studio with me.

They’ll say my name, and they’ll say my work is being judged. And the house is quiet, nobody’s there, but it sounds real. Like not just me thinking it… like somebody said it out loud. I’ll be trying to do one thing, and then I’m listening for it, and then I forget what I was even trying to say.
Do you think the voices you hear are real or just your imagination?

I don’t know… part of me wants to say it’s just my imagination, because that would make more sense, right? But when it happens, it sounds real. Like clear, like somebody is standing right there in my little studio.

I came in because I keep hearing them say my name, and saying my work is being judged, even when the house is quiet and nobody’s there. And then I’ll look around, or stop what I’m doing, and it’s like… I know nobody’s supposed to be there, but it doesn’t feel made up in that moment.
Have you noticed any big changes in how you're behaving or functioning in your daily life since the voices started?

Yeah… yes, it changed a lot. I was still trying to work, you know, doing my aide visits, and I used to be pretty good with keeping people’s routines straight — who needed what, writing the care notes, getting to the next place. But then I started missing shifts, and I’d mix up notes or forget what visit I was supposed to be organizing next. My job got… it got to where they were talking like I might not be able to keep it if I didn’t get myself together.

And outside of work, I kind of disappeared. I stopped going to my walking club, and I used to like those art talks at the library — they had one about watercolor once, or maybe it was collage, I don’t know — but I stopped going. Mostly I just stayed home by myself. It’s embarrassing, because I don’t want people seeing me like that.
Do the voices and the feeling of being judged happen all the time, or do they come and go?

It’s not like every single minute, no… but it keeps coming back. The voices and that feeling like my work is being watched or judged, that’s been going on for about nine months now.

I remember thinking at first maybe it was just stress from work, because people always have opinions about how you do things, you know… but it didn’t really go away. It’s been around since then, off and on, for months.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family since the voices and feelings of being judged started?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I pulled away from people. I stopped going to the walking club, and I used to go to those art talks at the library — they had one lady who did these little paintings, I think birds, or maybe flowers — and I just quit going.

And with work, that kind of spilled into everything too. I was missing aide shifts, mixing up the care notes, not keeping the visits straight like I used to. It made me feel ashamed, like people were noticing, so I mostly just stayed home by myself.
Do you believe the voices you hear are trying to tell you something important or warning you about something?

I don’t know if it’s important exactly… it feels important when it happens. Like they’re right there in my little studio, clear as somebody standing next to me, saying my name. And then they say my work is being judged.

It’s strange because the house can be completely quiet, nobody there, and I still hear it. Sometimes I start thinking, well maybe I forgot something from a visit, or maybe somebody’s upset with me, and then I get stuck on that. My neighbor has a loud TV sometimes too, so at first I thought maybe it was through the wall, but… no, it’s my name they’re saying.
Have you had to stop doing things you enjoy or had trouble keeping up with your work because of these voices and feelings of being judged?

Yeah… I did. I mean, I didn’t mean to stop everything, it just kind of happened. I quit going to my walking club, and those art talks at the library too — I used to like those, they had nice little talks, nothing fancy, but it got me out of the house.

And work got bad. My aide job was… it was in danger, I think. I missed shifts, and I mixed up the care notes, and I couldn’t keep the visits organized like I used to. I used to be pretty careful with that. Then I’d sit at home alone thinking about it, and it just made me feel worse.
Have you been doing things in a way that seems unusual or disorganized to other people?

Yeah… I think so. People have noticed, I’m pretty sure.

Like on client visits, I’d be there to do the usual things, and then I’d just… stop. Instead of doing what I was supposed to be doing, I’d start lining up the gloves, or the little pill cups, making them even, like in rows or patterns. Sometimes there’d be crochet scraps around — one lady had all these bits of yarn, real pretty colors, she made little blankets, my aunt used to crochet too — and I’d start arranging those too, like it meant something.

And then other times I’d just stand in the hallway staring, like I was waiting for… I don’t know, a signal or something. It sounds odd saying it out loud. I know that’s not how you’re supposed to act when you’re working in somebody’s home.
Do you have periods where the voices and feelings of being judged stop completely, or are they always present to some degree?

They’re not always loud every second, no… there are times it kind of quiets down, like if I’m washing dishes or the TV is on, though then I wonder if the TV is part of it, which is silly maybe. But it hasn’t really gone away gone away.

The voices and that feeling like my work is being watched or judged… that’s been going on about nine months now. Around there. I keep thinking back to when it started, and I get mixed up because I had that one client with the blue curtains, and then the schedule changed, and— anyway, it’s been months. Not just a few days.
Have you been acting in ways that seem strange or unusual to you or to other people lately?

Yeah… lately, yes. I mean, I don’t always realize it right when I’m doing it, but afterward I think, that must’ve looked strange.

Like when I’m on a client visit, I’ll be there to do the regular care things, and then I just… stop. I start lining up the gloves, or those little pill cups, making them even, like they have to sit a certain way. Sometimes if there’s crochet scraps around — my aunt used to keep bags of yarn like that, all different colors, she made these little squares and never finished half of them — I’ll start arranging those too, in patterns.

And then sometimes I’m just standing in the hallway, staring, like I’m waiting for some kind of signal to tell me what to do next. It feels embarrassing saying it, because I know people probably think, what is she doing?
Are there times when you don't hear the voices at all?

Not really… I mean, sometimes the apartment is quiet, like quiet enough I can hear the refrigerator clicking, and I’ll think maybe it’s stopped, but then I hear it again clear, like somebody’s right there in my little studio.

They’ll say my name, or say my work is being judged. And I look around because it feels like someone should be standing there, but nobody is. It’s strange because my neighbor’s TV comes through the wall sometimes, and I’ll think, is it that? But no… this is more clear than that. It’s like it’s in the room with me.
Have the voices and feelings of being judged been continuous for at least six months?

Yes… yes, it’s been at least that. I think about nine months now. The voices, and that feeling like my work is being watched or judged — it’s just been there.

I keep trying to place it by little things, like what client I had then or what season it was, and then I get sidetracked, but… yeah. It’s been going on for months, around nine months.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your physical activity level or movements since the voices started?

Yeah… my body just won’t settle sometimes. Like I get this rush of energy and I can’t sit down, even if it’s nighttime and I should be in bed.

I’ll clean my whole kitchen, then I’ll start painting — not one painting, like three different ones — and then I find yarn and start crocheting, like half a blanket before I even notice how long I’ve been doing it. My aunt used to crochet all the time, she had these colors that didn’t match but somehow looked nice together, and I think about that, and then I’m pulling out my own yarn.

And then I’ll be rewriting care schedules for work in the same night, moving things around, making lists… it’s like my hands have to keep going. I don’t feel like I can just sit still.

doctor.question: Do you have periods where the voices and feelings of being judged stop completely, or are they always present to some degree?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The voices and fixed fears about my work being watched have been happening for about 9 months now.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the persistence/course of the voices and feelings of being judged, which most directly relates to how long the psychotic symptoms have been present.

patient.answer:
They’re not always loud every second, no… there are times it kind of quiets down, like if I’m washing dishes or the TV is on, though then I wonder if the TV is part of it, which is silly maybe. But it hasn’t really gone away gone away.

The voices and that feeling like my work is being watched or judged… that’s been going on about nine months now. Around there. I keep thinking back to when it started, and I get mixed up because I had that one client with the blue curtains, and then the schedule changed, and— anyway, it’s been months. Not just a few days.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of disorganized behavior
doctor.question: Have you been acting in ways that seem strange or unusual to you or to other people lately?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: There have been times on client visits where I’d stop what I was supposed to be doing and start lining up gloves, pill cups, and crochet scraps in patterns, or stand in the hallway staring like I was waiting for some signal.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about acting in strange or unusual ways, which directly matches disorganized or abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
Yeah… lately, yes. I mean, I don’t always realize it right when I’m doing it, but afterward I think, that must’ve looked strange.

Like when I’m on a client visit, I’ll be there to do the regular care things, and then I just… stop. I start lining up the gloves, or those little pill cups, making them even, like they have to sit a certain way. Sometimes if there’s crochet scraps around — my aunt used to keep bags of yarn like that, all different colors, she made these little squares and never finished half of them — I’ll start arranging those too, in patterns.

And then sometimes I’m just standing in the hallway, staring, like I’m waiting for some kind of signal to tell me what to do next. It feels embarrassing saying it, because I know people probably think, what is she doing?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's symptoms are persistent or episodic
doctor.question: Are there times when you don't hear the voices at all?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing voices clear as somebody standing in my little studio, saying my name and telling me my work is being judged, even when the house is quiet and nobody is there.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about whether the patient ever stops hearing voices, which concerns hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Not really… I mean, sometimes the apartment is quiet, like quiet enough I can hear the refrigerator clicking, and I’ll think maybe it’s stopped, but then I hear it again clear, like somebody’s right there in my little studio.

They’ll say my name, or say my work is being judged. And I look around because it feels like someone should be standing there, but nobody is. It’s strange because my neighbor’s TV comes through the wall sometimes, and I’ll think, is it that? But no… this is more clear than that. It’s like it’s in the room with me.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's symptoms meet the duration criteria for a schizophrenia diagnosis
doctor.question: Have the voices and feelings of being judged been continuous for at least six months?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The voices and fixed fears about my work being watched have been happening for about 9 months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the voices and feelings of being judged have lasted continuously for at least six months, which directly concerns the duration of psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yes… yes, it’s been at least that. I think about nine months now. The voices, and that feeling like my work is being watched or judged — it’s just been there.

I keep trying to place it by little things, like what client I had then or what season it was, and then I get sidetracked, but… yeah. It’s been going on for months, around nine months.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of significant psychomotor symptoms
doctor.question: Have you experienced any significant changes in your physical activity level or movements since the voices started?

target_item.name: Increased_Activity
target_item.manifestation: I get so much energy that I’ll clean my whole kitchen, start three paintings, crochet half a blanket, and rewrite care schedules all in the same night without being able to sit down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about significant changes in physical activity level since the voices started, which most directly matches increased activity and energy.

patient.answer:
Yeah… my body just won’t settle sometimes. Like I get this rush of energy and I can’t sit down, even if it’s nighttime and I should be in bed.

I’ll clean my whole kitchen, then I’ll start painting — not one painting, like three different ones — and then I find yarn and start crocheting, like half a blanket before I even notice how long I’ve been doing it. My aunt used to crochet all the time, she had these colors that didn’t match but somehow looked nice together, and I think about that, and then I’m pulling out my own yarn.

And then I’ll be rewriting care schedules for work in the same night, moving things around, making lists… it’s like my hands have to keep going. I don’t feel like I can just sit still.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a mix of psychotic symptoms, including hearing voices that are clear and seem real, and disorganized thinking and behavior, which have been continuous for at least six months. The voices comment on the patient's work being judged, and the patient believes they are being watched. These symptoms, combined with the patient's disorganized speech and behavior, such as lining up objects or staring, suggest a diagnosis of acute and transient psychotic disorder (F23).
